questions.q: Per this lesson, why are risks identified in Chapter 1 instead of waiting until after the detailed design is finished?
options: Because many important risks are already visible once the current state, stakeholders, and vision are understood, without needing the detailed design first
Because risk identification is legally required before any Salesforce project can begin
Because Chapter 1 has extra time available that later chapters don't
Because risks discovered during design are not valid and must be ignored
questions.explain: Every risk in LTV Global's register traces back to a fact already established earlier in Chapter 1 (current state, stakeholders, vision) — none of them required the detailed design to become visible.

questions.q: In the risk register, which risk is rated high impact but only medium likelihood, described as serious if it happened but avoidable with design discipline?
options: Governance sprawl across four business units
LedgerPoint's batch-only nature delaying financial visibility
GDPR and EMEA data-residency obligations being violated
A single integration user owning all dealer-synced records
questions.explain: The GDPR/data-residency risk is explicitly called out as high impact but medium (avoidable) likelihood, in contrast to governance sprawl, which is rated lower impact but higher likelihood.

questions.q: What mitigation does this lesson assign to the risk of a single integration user owning all dealer-synced records?
options: Replacing Meridian ERP with a new system
Queue-based record ownership instead of a single integration-user owner
Moving all dealer data into LedgerPoint instead of Salesforce
Disabling the dealer integration entirely
questions.explain: The mitigation named for the ownership/data-skew risk is queue-based record ownership rather than concentrating ownership in one integration user — detailed further in the large data volume lesson.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say governance sprawl (risk 6) is rated high likelihood despite a lower impact rating than several other risks?
options: Because governance problems always cause a single dramatic failure
Because GDPR violations are a direct cause of governance sprawl
Because governance sprawl has no real consequence and is included only for completeness
Because four business units left alone without deliberate intervention are almost certain to diverge over time, even though each individual divergence is less catastrophic
questions.explain: Governance sprawl compounds slowly and is nearly certain without intervention, since four independent business units will naturally diverge — which is why it is rated high likelihood even though no single instance is as dramatic as some other risks.

questions.q: What does this lesson say happens to the Chapter 1 risk register later in the course?
options: It is formalized with updated assessments in Chapter 5's deliverables, and is likely to resurface in the Chapter 6 Architecture Review Board defense
It is discarded once the detailed design begins
It is replaced entirely by a new, unrelated risk list in Chapter 4
It only matters for this single lesson and is never referenced again
questions.explain: Lesson 25 formalizes this same risk list into a deliverable risk register, and the lesson notes the Architecture Review Board in Chapter 6 will likely question the architect directly on at least one of these risks.
